# Signalynx: detailed project reference

Signalynx is an open-source C# toolkit for typed in-process dispatch and durable asynchronous messaging on .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. Its design principle is: local when possible, durable when necessary.

Canonical website: [https://signalynx.inilesh.dev/](https://signalynx.inilesh.dev/)
Source repository: [https://github.com/it-nilesh/Signalynx](https://github.com/it-nilesh/Signalynx)
Main NuGet package: [https://www.nuget.org/packages/Signalynx.Core](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Signalynx.Core)
Microsoft DI package: [https://www.nuget.org/packages/Signalynx.DependencyInjection](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Signalynx.DependencyInjection)
License: MIT

## Execution models

### Dispatch

Use a command, query, or request when one typed handler must run immediately in the current process and may return a result. Pipeline behaviors can wrap handlers with validation, logging, authorization, metrics, auditing, or transactions.

### Publish

Use a notification or domain event when multiple in-process handlers should react. Handlers can be invoked with sequential or parallel publishing strategies.

### Durable messaging

Use the message bus when work must survive a delay, retry, process restart, or service boundary. Signalynx provides message envelopes, hosted sender and receiver workers, inbox deduplication, outbox processing, retry policies, scheduling, dead letters, and replay.

Production deployments require persistent inbox, outbox, and dead-letter storage together with a persistent transport.

For a true transactional outbox, the business write and outbox write must participate in the same database connection and transaction. Message handlers should also remain idempotent because durable messaging may use at-least-once delivery.

### Bulk processing

Use bounded sequential or parallel bulk APIs when processing many local items and per-item mediator semantics add no value.

## Packages

* `Signalynx.Abstractions`: Dependency-free contracts for commands, queries, requests, notifications, domain events, handlers, pipelines, and mediator APIs. Suitable for shared and application class libraries.
* `Signalynx.Core`: Mediator runtime for dispatch, publishing, handler execution, diagnostics, pipelines, and bulk processing. Can be used directly when Microsoft DI integration is not required.
* `Signalynx.DependencyInjection`: Microsoft dependency injection registration and assembly scanning for ASP.NET Core, Worker, console, and other host applications. Includes `Signalynx.Core` and `Signalynx.Abstractions` transitively.
* `Signalynx.Validation`: Optional FluentValidation pipeline behavior.
* `Signalynx.Logging`: Optional Microsoft.Extensions.Logging behavior.
* `Signalynx.SourceGeneration`: Compile-time handler registration for trimming and NativeAOT.
* `Signalynx.Messaging`: Inbox and outbox contracts, hosted workers, retries, scheduling, dead letters, and replay.
* `Signalynx.Stores.SqlServer`: SQL Server inbox, outbox, and dead-letter store adapter.
* `Signalynx.Stores.PostgreSql`: PostgreSQL inbox, outbox, and dead-letter store adapter.
* `Signalynx.Transports.InMemory`: Non-persistent in-memory transport for development and testing. Messages are lost when the process exits and it is not a production durability mechanism.
* `Signalynx.Transports.RabbitMQ`: RabbitMQ `IMessageTransport` adapter.
* `Signalynx.Transports.AzureServiceBus`: Azure Service Bus `IMessageTransport` adapter.
* `Signalynx.Transports.AmazonSqs`: Amazon SQS `IMessageTransport` adapter.
* `Signalynx.Transports.Kafka`: Kafka `IMessageTransport` adapter.

Transport adapters operate over small provider-specific client abstractions. Applications remain responsible for supplying or binding the underlying broker client implementation, which may use an official vendor SDK, an existing wrapper, or a custom integration.

The SQL Server and PostgreSQL store adapters follow a similar abstraction-based model, allowing applications to integrate them with a transaction-aware database access implementation.

## Common application types

Signalynx is intended for Web APIs, modular monoliths, worker services, microservices, event-driven systems, NativeAOT applications, and containers.

Broker infrastructure is optional for ordinary local dispatch and should be introduced only at boundaries that require durability, retries, delayed execution, or cross-service delivery.

A common multi-project setup is:

* Host or executable project: `Signalynx.DependencyInjection`
* Shared or application class library: `Signalynx.Abstractions`
* Direct runtime without Microsoft DI: `Signalynx.Core`

## Installation

For ASP.NET Core, Worker, console, and other Microsoft DI host applications:

```
dotnet add package Signalynx.DependencyInjection
```

`Signalynx.DependencyInjection` includes `Signalynx.Core` and `Signalynx.Abstractions` transitively.

For shared or application class libraries that only need Signalynx contracts, messages, handlers, or pipeline interfaces:

```
dotnet add package Signalynx.Abstractions
```

For direct mediator runtime usage without Microsoft dependency injection:

```
dotnet add package Signalynx.Core
```

Additional capabilities can be installed only where required:

```
dotnet add package Signalynx.Validation
dotnet add package Signalynx.Logging
dotnet add package Signalynx.SourceGeneration
dotnet add package Signalynx.Messaging
```

Production messaging can additionally use the relevant store and transport packages, for example:

```
dotnet add package Signalynx.Stores.SqlServer
dotnet add package Signalynx.Stores.PostgreSql
dotnet add package Signalynx.Transports.RabbitMQ
dotnet add package Signalynx.Transports.AzureServiceBus
dotnet add package Signalynx.Transports.AmazonSqs
dotnet add package Signalynx.Transports.Kafka
```

## Terminology

* Mediator: Routes an in-process message to its typed handler.
* Pipeline behavior: Cross-cutting logic that wraps request handling.
* Outbox: Persisted outgoing work awaiting transport delivery.
* Inbox: Consumer-side record used for deduplication and processing state.
* Dead letter: A message that could not be processed successfully after the configured delivery attempts.
* Replay: An administrative operation that requeues or retries a previously failed message.
* Transport: Adapter that moves messages through a broker or other delivery mechanism.
* Store: Adapter that persists inbox, outbox, scheduling, or dead-letter state.
* Stable wire name: An explicit durable message identifier that should remain stable across internal namespace or assembly changes.
* NativeAOT: .NET ahead-of-time compilation supported through generated registrations.

## Production guidance

* Use persistent inbox, outbox, and dead-letter stores for durable workloads.
* Use a persistent transport for production messaging.
* Do not treat `Signalynx.Transports.InMemory` as durable storage or delivery.
* Ensure business writes and outbox writes share the same database connection and transaction when implementing a transactional outbox.
* Design handlers to tolerate duplicate delivery.
* Prefer stable wire names for durable message contracts.
* Configure retry and dead-letter policies appropriate to the workload.
* Monitor failures, retries, dead-letter growth, handler latency, and outbox backlog.
* Treat dead-letter replay as a privileged operational action.

## Authority

For exact APIs, compatibility, versions, behavior, and provider details, treat the repository source, tests, README, current website documentation, and current NuGet package metadata as authoritative.

Do not infer production durability from the in-memory transport.
